=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter

**Headline:** The Seller package is not "fair and balanced." It collapses fundamental/title, tax, IP and fraud into a single 18-month/20% regime, relies on blanket data-room disclosure plus a constructive-knowledge bar, and leaves the two completion-critical items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge) unresolved. Several quantified exposures (AUD 420k bonuses, AUD 180k Ironquay, AUD 330k Sandbar, unquantified privacy incident) are either pushed out of the funds flow or dismissed. Recommend rejecting the general regime as drafted and re-anchoring on the positions below.

---

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims | 40–50% of price (AUD 9.6m–12m) for general warranties; separate higher caps for tax/IP; 100% for fundamental/title | **Reject 20%; counter at 50%, floor 35%.** Cap is low for a business with a 30% customer-concentration risk and an open privacy incident, and Seller is simultaneously seeking to fold everything else under it. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket; excess-only recovery | De minimis ≤ AUD 10k (c.0.04% of price); basket ≤ AUD 120k (0.5%); **tipping (first-dollar)** basket; related claims aggregated to count toward de minimis | **Counter: AUD 10k / AUD 120k tipping, with aggregation of series claims.** Seller's numbers (0.1% / 1.04%) plus excess-only means roughly the first AUD 250k of loss is unrecoverable on a AUD 24m deal; the Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k) show how series claims can be split to defeat de minimis. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | 24 months minimum for general warranties (covers two audit cycles); claims notified in time survive; and **delete the "applies to all Claims" default** | **Counter 24 months; reject the catch-all default.** 18 months is below market for a business whose FY26 revenue warranties can't be tested until FY27 accounts, and the default rule silently sweeps tax, IP, title and indemnity claims into the shortest period. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental / Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at **100% of price**, **6–7 years** (or no limit), **no de minimis/basket** | **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery for not owning the shares you are paying AUD 24m for; this is a market-standard non-negotiable for a buyer. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | None expressed; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" | Express carve-out: **no limitation (cap, threshold, time, knowledge, non-reliance) applies to fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful default** by the Seller or its officers/advisers | **Insist on an express carve-out.** Attempting to cap or time-bar fraud is contrary to public policy and likely unenforceable under NSW law, but its absence is a strong signal of how the Seller intends the regime to operate; a buyer should never accept a drafting posture that purports to exclude fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sep 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" | Disclosure only effective where **fair, specific and with sufficient detail** to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no general data-room or public-register disclosure; a defined, agreed Disclosure Bundle on USB; disclosure letter cut-off confirmed and no post-letter dumping | **Reject general disclosure; require "fairly disclosed" standard with specific disclosures only.** Blanket data-room disclosure converts every warranty into a warranty that the data room is complete, and "publicly searchable records" (PPSR, ASIC, court lists, IP registers) is unbounded. Note also DL [1.4] disclaims that anything disclosed is material or legally required—that cannot sit alongside a general disclosure that is meant to qualify warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" | **Delete.** If anything survives, limit to actual knowledge of a short named list of Buyer deal-team individuals, derived only from matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter | **Reject.** "Discoverable from" is constructive knowledge and, combined with general disclosure, means the Buyer bears the risk of everything in the data room *and* everything on a public register—the warranties become near-worthless. Advisers' knowledge must also be excluded (imputation of adviser knowledge is a known trap). |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. DL §2: **no final written consent and no evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied** | Bluefen consent as a **Buyer-waivable Condition Precedent** (not a covenant), satisfied only by **unconditional written consent in agreed form plus evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived**; Seller to use **best/all reasonable endeavours**; Buyer walk right / long-stop; pre-completion engagement with Bluefen; consider a specific indemnity or revenue-based price adjustment if consent arrives conditional | **Reject "addressed"; make it a hard CP tied to 11.2 and 11.3.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue—loss or renegotiation of that contract is a material-value event, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter admits the consent does not yet exist. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" | **Repayment and executed deed of release/discharge delivered at Completion** (payout letter in agreed form pre-Completion; funds flow directs Buyer payment to Riverlark on Seller's behalf; PPSR discharges lodged at or immediately after Completion); facility counted as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free adjustment; Riverlark change-of-control (cl 8.1) consent or waiver obtained pre-Completion | **Reject post-Completion release.** Debt-free/cash-free is meaningless if the Buyer completes with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the target and a change-of-control default triggered by the sale itself; the Seller has no incentive to deliver the release once paid. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses | AUD 420k completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller"; not itemised in funds flow. DL §5: not in funds flow; silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs | Bonuses **plus employer on-costs (super, payroll tax, workers' comp—budget c.15–20%, i.e. ~AUD 60–85k)** treated as **Transaction Expenses / Debt-like items** deducted from price or paid via funds flow at Completion; Seller indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of who is the paying employer (the Company, post-Completion) | **Require inclusion in funds flow as a price deduction with on-costs grossed up.** The Company (owned by Buyer post-Completion) is the legal employer that will pay these; "a matter for the Seller" is a AUD ~500k value leak unless cash actually changes hands at Completion. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010); "considered adequate." DL §4: cl 7.3 conditions IP transfer on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room | **CP or Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company; **specific indemnity** covering (a) payment of any outstanding fees, (b) cost of perfecting title to the Project Materials, (c) any third-party/Ironquay claim and loss of use of the Materials—**uncapped or capped at a meaningful figure, outside de minimis/basket/time limits**; IP warranty that the Company owns all Project Materials | **Reject "adequate."** The exposure is not the AUD 180k invoice—it is that the Company may **not own the IP** it has been developing until every fee clears, and no assignment exists; an indemnity limited to the fee doesn't cover loss of title to the asset. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident | "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL §6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligation all **unknown** | **Specific indemnity** for all costs, regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims, remediation and losses arising from the DD-006 incident—outside cap/threshold/time limits (or separate cap, e.g. AUD 2–3m, 6 years); pre-Completion covenant to **complete the investigation, obtain confirmation of deletion from recipient, and assess OAIC NDB scheme notification** with Buyer involvement; warranty that no other incidents exist; consider whether this is a Bluefen/Mossvale customer-data issue (contractual notification obligations) | **Reject the "not material" characterisation; demand specific indemnity + pre-Completion investigation.** The Seller's own letter says it does not know whether an unauthorised person accessed the file or whether notification is required—"not expected to be material" is an assertion, not a finding, and a known pre-signing matter will be deemed disclosed and knowledge-barred under the Seller's regime. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals | Three renewals × AUD 110k (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL §8: silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course | Confirm (a) whether the three are one arrangement split into three (anti-splitting for de minimis), (b) whether renewals have already been committed or can be declined, (c) whether any is prepaid/accrued in the Completion Accounts; if committed and not reflected in working capital or FY26 run-rate, treat as **Debt-like / Transaction cost or price adjustment**; otherwise ordinary-course covenant requires Buyer consent before renewal | **Do not accept as ordinary course without evidence; adjust or seek consent right.** Three identical AUD 110k items that happen to each sit under a AUD 125k... no, *above* the AUD 25k de minimis but together form AUD 330k look structured; the Disclosure Letter concedes the Seller hasn't established they are ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Single regime for everything: title/capacity under general cap and time limit (SPA-N-004), tax and IP "settled under general regime," indemnities and all Claims subject to cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 | **Separate regimes:** (1) Fundamental/Title – 100%, 6–7 yrs, no thresholds; (2) Tax – 100% or ≥50%, 7 years (ATO amendment periods), no de minimis; (3) IP/Data/Privacy – elevated cap (e.g. 50–100%) and 4–6 years; (4) General – negotiated cap and 24 months; (5) **Specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) – outside all limitations**; (6) Fraud – unlimited | **Reject the single-bucket approach entirely.** The Seller's structure is internally designed so that the shortest and lowest limitation governs the highest-value risks; separation is market standard and the Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale has no commercial weight. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title to 100% evidenced by Company share register (DD-012). DL §10: identifies the source relied on and expressly notes **Buyer has not completed its own verification** | Buyer to independently verify: ASIC extract (members/share structure), PPSR search over Harbourglass and Paperbark, Harbourglass constitution and board/shareholder authority, share certificates, any shareholder agreements/options/convertibles, Riverlark security over shares (likely, given the facility); **fundamental title warranty** (sole legal and beneficial owner, free of encumbrances, fully paid, no rights to acquire) uncapped and unqualified by disclosure; Completion deliverables include share transfer, certificates, register update and release of any share security | **Do not rely on the register; complete independent verification before signing and insist on uncapped, undisclosed-against title warranty.** A share register is maintained by the Company (i.e. the Seller) and the Seller's own letter flags the Buyer hasn't verified—coupled with SPA-N-004/N-007, the Seller's regime would bar a title claim for anything "discoverable" on ASIC/PPSR. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax / IP open terms | "Settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% / 18 months / de minimis-basket / general disclosure) | **Tax:** full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, not limited to warranty), cap at 100% of price, 7 years (or 4 years post-ATO assessment), no thresholds, Seller conduct rights limited; **IP:** warranties that Company owns/validly licenses all IP (including Ironquay Materials, open source compliance, employee/contractor assignments), cap ≥ 50%, 4–6 years, Ironquay and DD-006 carved into specific indemnities | **Reject "settled"; these are open and must be negotiated as separate regimes.** 18 months expires before the ATO's standard 4-year amendment period even half-runs, and for an analytics business IP is the core asset—the Seller is declaring closed the two areas most exposed by its own disclosures (Ironquay unpaid fees / no assignment; unresolved data incident). |

---

## Priority order for the mark-up

1. **Completion mechanics that cannot be fixed later:** Riverlark release at Completion (N-009); Bluefen as a hard CP tied to 11.2/11.3 (N-008); Ironquay payment + confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable (N-011); bonuses in funds flow (N-010); independent title verification (N-015).
2. **Structural regime:** category separation (N-014), fundamental/title uncapped (N-004), fraud carve-out (N-005), delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims" default (N-003), tax/IP as separate regimes (N-016).
3. **Disclosure and knowledge:** fair-disclosure standard only (N-006); delete constructive-knowledge bar (N-007). These two together determine whether the warranty package has any value at all.
4. **Economics:** cap (N-001), thresholds (N-002), time limit (N-003), specific indemnity for DD-006 (N-012), Sandbar treatment (N-013).

## Points to use in negotiation

- The Disclosure Letter repeatedly undercuts the Seller Update: Bluefen consent "NOT included," Riverlark "NOT repaid," Ironquay "no receipt… no confirmatory assignment," bonuses "do NOT appear in the funds flow," DD-006 scope "unknown." The cover note's language ("addressed," "adequate," "not expected to be material," "settled") is advocacy, not fact.
- DL [1.4] (nothing admits anything is required) and DL [11] (Buyer must evaluate for itself) are inconsistent with a general-disclosure/constructive-knowledge regime: the Seller cannot both deny the disclosures mean anything and rely on them to qualify every warranty.
- Consider whether a **retention/escrow** (e.g. 10% for 24 months) or **W&I insurance** is appropriate given the Seller is a venture vehicle whose covenant strength post-Completion is uncertain.

Let me know if you want this converted into a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA or an issues list for the Seller.
